6.3 Legal, Social, Ethical and Professional Issues 
6.3.1 Legal Issues 
The Data Protection Act 2018 and the General Data Protection Regulation 
(GDPR) are critical considerations while collecting and storing personal data 
within an eLearning application (UK Government, n.d.). Since the application 
focuses on GCSE students, whom are typically are under the age of 17, it is vital 
to implement measures to parental consent when necessary, such as within the 
study. The application must adhere to these laws by ensuring robust data 
protection strategies such as encrypting data and only storing information for as 
long as it is needed. The application and study get around many of these issues 
by simply not collecting any personal data and ensuring that the data collected is 
handled with the upmost importance. 
The Copyright, Designs and Patents Act 1988, the applications content including 
educational material, graphics, and text, all must either be created by the author 
of this document or be licensed by the appropriate person, or in this projects 
case follow any fair dealing exceptions for educational purposes (UK 
Government, n.d.). Meaning that before any third-party content can be used, it 
must be checked for its licensing. 
Ensuring the application is accessible to all students, including ones with 
disabilities, comes under the Equality Act 2010 (Gavin, 2021). This requires the 
applications design to be usable for people with a range of disabilities, enforcing 
design considerations such as high contrast ratios and accessible navigation. For 
this the application followed the guidelines by (WCAG, 2023), to acceptable 
contrast ratios, and utilises Androids built in accessibility features (Google, n.d.). 
In accordance with the Computer Misuse Act 1990, the application must be 
secure against unauthorised access attacks (UK Government, 2023).
